uncited: Switch-NeRF++ is a large-scale neural radiance field method that employs a Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture to efficiently render heterogeneous urban scenes.
It solves the scalability problem of HashGrid Neural Fields by routing 3D points to specialized hash experts based on local scene complexity, thereby balancing memory usage and rendering accuracy.

It differs from standard HashNeRF by introducing a learned gating mechanism that selects a single expert per point, and from Switch-NeRF by upgrading the expert capacity and resolution scaling for higher fidelity in massive environments.
The method uses a HashGate and $N$ Hash Experts.
Their base resolutions $\{r\}$ are logarithmically spaced in $[16, 512]$.
*   **Space Contraction:** To handle unbounded space, points are normalized into a unit sphere.
*   **Time Complexity:** Dominated by the hash lookups in the gating network and the selected expert.
Since only one expert is selected per point, the per-point cost is comparable to a single HashGrid lookup plus MLP inference, rather than summing all experts.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Determined by the sum of the hash table sizes of all $N$ experts.
Switch-NeRF++ was developed to address the limitations of previous neural radiance field methods in large-scale urban reconstruction.
It builds on the HashNeRF architecture and the Switch-NeRF MoE approach.
